title: Question 2
stem:
The variation with time t of the velocity v of two cars P and Q is shown in Fig. 2.1.
The cars travel in the same direction along a straight road.
Car P passes car Q at time t = 0.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: The speed limit for cars on the road is 100 km $h^{-1}$. State and explain whether car Q exceeds the speed limit.

markscheme_points.text: 30 m s-1 = 108 km h-1 or 100 km h-1 = 28 m s-1 and so exceeds speed limit

hints: Hint 1: Consider the physical mechanism underlying this process based on physical principles and measurement.
parts.proper_answer: 30 m s-1 = 108 km h-1 or 100 km h-1 = 28 m s-1 and so exceeds speed limit

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Determine the distance between the two cars at time t = 12 s.
distance = $m $

markscheme_points.text: distance travelled by Q = ½ × 12 × 30 (= 180 m)
distance travelled by P = ½ × (20 + 24) × 12 (= 264 m)

hints: Hint 1: Identify the given data from the problem and recall the governing equation connecting these quantities using physical principles and measurement.
Hint 2: Rearrange the formula to isolate the required quantity before substituting numerical values with correct powers of ten.
Hint 3: Check your intermediate calculation steps carefully and ensure your final answer is stated to an appropriate number of significant figures with correct SI units.
parts.proper_answer: distance travelled by Q = ½ × 12 × 30 (= 180 m); distance travelled by P = ½ × (20 + 24) × 12 (= 264 m); distance between cars = 264 - 180 = 84 m

parts.text:
From time t = 12 s, the velocity of each car remains constant at its value at t = 12 s.
Determine the time t at which car Q passes car P.
